title: He Walked by Night

evidence.note: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Motion Pictures Jan-Dec 1948 (Vol 2 Nos 1-2). In the Jul-Dec listings I read, the title sequence runs 'HECTOR'S HECTIC LIFE' then 'HER FAVORITE POOLS', and no 'HE WALKED BY NIGHT' registration appears there. The Jan-Jun claimant index entries for Pathe Industries (Eagle-Lion's claimant name on other 1948 films) do not list it either. I did not read the whole volume, and I found no LP number for the film. The 1949 volume and the 1940-1949 cumulative were not checked.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Motion Pictures 1948

evidence.note: CCE Motion Pictures 1975 volume. The H title index runs 'Heterosexual intercourse' then 'He who digs a grave', with no 'He walked by night' between them. I did not read the renewal section itself.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Motion Pictures 1975

evidence.note: CCE Motion Pictures 1976 volume. The H title index runs '...He's in again', 'Hidden danger', with no 'He walked by night'. The index has an 'Eagle-Lion Films, Inc.' line on page 118, a renewal page, but the OCR dropped the title and I could not identify the film. That entry is unresolved and needs a human check of the page image. I did not read the renewal section itself.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Motion Pictures 1976

evidence.note: CCE Motion Pictures 1977 volume. The H title index runs 'He's gone away' then 'Hickmar Productions', with no 'He walked by night'. I did not read the renewal section itself.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Motion Pictures 1977

evidence.note: The music is credited to Leonid Raab. It is a sound film with an original recorded score, so the score normally shares the film's own copyright status. That status is not settled, so the score is not settled either. I did not check any separate music registration.

The screenplay is by John C. Higgins and Crane Wilbur, from a story by Crane Wilbur. It is loosely based on the 1945-1946 crimes of Erwin 'Machine-Gun' Walker. I found no published book as the source. The story layer therefore rests on the film's own copyright and its status is unresolved. Real events themselves are not copyrightable.

I found no documented archival restoration. The Internet Archive holds several uploads, including titles marked 'colorized', and an upload of a TCM broadcast. Colorization and broadcast graphics are added material and can carry their own protection. I did not open those items.
evidence.source: Internet Archive search for the title

renewal_search.negative_result: INCOMPLETE. I read the H title index of the CCE Motion Pictures volumes for 1975, 1976 and 1977 and found no 'He walked by night'. I also checked the Jul-Dec 1948 title listings and the Pathe Industries claimant lists, and the film is not there. I did not read the renewal sections themselves. The 1976 index has one unidentified Eagle-Lion Films renewal entry on page 118. No Copyright Office public-catalog search was run. This is not a confirmed absence of renewal.

editorial:
He Walked by Night is a 79-minute Eagle-Lion crime picture released in Los Angeles on November 24, 1948. Bryan Foy and Robert Kane produced it. Alfred L. Werker is the credited director, and Anthony Mann is uncredited. John Alton shot it. Richard Basehart plays the burglar and cop-killer Roy Morgan, and Scott Brady and Roy Roberts lead the police hunt. It is loosely based on the 1945-1946 crimes of Erwin 'Machine-Gun' Walker. Jack Webb appears in it, and he met the police advisor Marty Wynn on this production, a meeting that inspired the radio show Dragnet. A reuser gets a police procedural with Alton's high-contrast photography, and the sewer chase near the end is the part people clip.

The rights trap is that the film's copyright status is unresolved in this dossier. I could not find a 1948 registration for the title in the Jul-Dec catalog pages I read, and I found no title entry in the 1975-1977 indexes. But I did not read the renewal sections, and the 1976 index holds an unidentified Eagle-Lion renewal entry on page 118. Several Internet Archive copies carry a public domain mark, and Wikipedia says the film is public domain. Neither is a primary source. Check the page-118 entry and run the Copyright Office search before you rely on the print. Avoid the colorized uploads in any case, because colorization is added material.
faq: Is He Walked by Night in the public domain?

Not confirmed here. The Internet Archive copies carry a public domain mark and Wikipedia calls the film public domain, but neither is a copyright record. I found no title entry in the 1975-1977 catalog indexes. I did not read the renewal sections, and the 1976 index has one unidentified Eagle-Lion renewal entry on page 118. Check that entry and the Copyright Office public catalog first.
Can I use the Internet Archive copy in my own video?

The film's status is still open (see above). The score by Leonid Raab and the story are tied to the film's own copyright status. Colorized or broadcast-captured uploads add material that may be protected, so prefer an uncolored upload such as He_Walked_by_Night_1948 and confirm its provenance.
